=== Revolutionary War ===
In August 1776 Ebenezer enlisted for one year on the Continental establishment. He served as a private in Captain Timothy Clement's company of Colonel Pierse Long's regiment of the New Hampshire line and was discharged at Stillwater, New York, in August 1777.<ref name="curpension">"U.S., Revolutionary War Pension and Bounty-Land Warrant Application Files, 1800-1900", database with images, Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1995/records/14945 : accessed 18 November 2026), Ebenezer Currier, pension file W. 724 (widow Mercy), Vermont; declaration of 23 April 1818, pension cards, and certified record of his marriage to Mercy Quimby, 14 Nov 1816 (images 47-56); citing NARA microfilm M804, roll 715.</ref> Living at Andover, New Hampshire, in reduced circumstances, he applied for a pension on 23 April 1818 under the Act of 18 March 1818. He was pensioned at eight dollars a month as "Ebenezer Currier 2d", and from March 1831 his payments were sent to Norwich, Windsor County, Vermont.<ref name="curpension"/>

On 14 November 1816, Ebenezer Currier of Andover married Mrs Mercy Quimby of Springfield, New Hampshire. As his widow, Mercy received a pension from 3 February 1853. She died on 21 November 1855.<ref name="curpension"/>

=== Research Notes ===
* A second Ebenezer Currier of New Hampshire also drew a Revolutionary pension (file S. 45715); that is why this Ebenezer was called "2d". The New Hampshire rolls of 1777-1783 (1st Battalion) probably belong to the other man, because this Ebenezer said he was discharged in 1777.<ref name="curnhroll">"New Hampshire, U.S., Revolutionary War Records, 1675-1835", database, Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61902/records/21684 : accessed 18 November 2026), Ebenezer Currier, private, 14 Jan 1777, New Hampshire muster rolls.</ref>
* An Ebenezer Currier of Amesbury served in Capt. John Currier's company of minute-men in Col. Isaac Merrill's regiment in 1775. This could be either Ebenezer or his father [[Currier-44|Ebenezer Currier]] (born 1723), and the record does not say which.
